newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids gain again with spot gas, crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids gain again with spot gas, crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices continued to gain ground Tuesday in moderate trade, with strong East Coast city gate gas prices and firmer crude still supporting the complex despite the lack of utility demand.

"It's unfortunate that electric generation is not that high because any generation favors six oil now, not gas," said one cash trader, noting healthy utility buy programs this month have helped firm the fuel oil market despite the lack of cooling load.
Surging gas prices this month, up more than 22 percent since late July, have encouraged some fuel switching to cheaper resid, traders said.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent firmed 25 cents to $16.25-50 a barrel, with September one percent paper up 10-15 cents to $16.40-60 with firmer crude. October paper was quoted at $16.70-85, with December pegged at $17.25-50.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour, still well supported by a New York utility's 850,000 barrel August buy program, gained 25 cents to the $18.50-75 range.

High sulphurs in New York climbed 10-25 cents, with 2.2 percent now quoted at $15.35-60 or higher. Traders said 50,000 barrels of prompt NYH 380 CST material (three percent max sulphur) sold at $15.75.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent gained a quarter to $15.50, while one percent was 30 cents higher at $16.25.

New York city gate gas prices firmed a couple of cents Tuesday to the mid-$2.70s/mmBtu, or $17.33 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also was slightly higher in the mid-$2.50s/mmBtu, or about $16.07 a barrel.
